topic: How to Open a Brokerage Account
source_evidence: Account Maintenance Fees - a monthly, quarterly, or annual fee that a broker-dealer may charge you for certain brokerage accounts below a certain dollar threshold to keep these accounts open at the brokerage. ... Wire or Transfer Fees - fees a broker-dealer may charge you to wire money from your brokerage account or to transfer assets or cash to another broker-dealer.
answer: Before opening a brokerage account, review which account fees may apply and how much they cost. A broker may charge a maintenance fee—often monthly, quarterly, or annually—for certain accounts below a specified dollar threshold. Other possible fees include inactivity fees, account-closing fees, and fees for wiring money or transferring assets or cash to another broker. Fees vary among firms, so ask your broker which charges apply to the account you are considering. If you later transfer an existing account, check whether the new broker accepts all your securities; selling securities that cannot be transferred may involve commissions or other fees, and your former account may have taxes, penalties, or restrictions.
